messages.subject: MVPA analysis in children
parts:
Hi all!

I am analyzing data from children aged 6-17y, and the outcome of my interest is MVPA over a week. Following the Whitehall II Study reference, I would like to retain activity lasting at least 1 min for which 80% of the activity satisfied the 191.6mg threshold criteria (children).

I am aware of:
- children threshold criteria for MVPA (based on VT Hildebrand M, VAN Hees VT et al. Med Sci Sports Exerc.2014); 
- the equation to calculate MVPA over a week when less than 7 valid days of data are available:
 (5xmean daily weekday MVPA time + 2x mean daily week-end MVPA time)/7 (based on Whitehall II Study Menai M, van Hees VT et al. Scientific Reports 2017) 

Therefore I plan to use part 2_daysummary.csv, to sum up for a single day of MVPA.: 

MVPA_E5S_B1M80%_T191.6_ENMO_0-24hr + MVPA_E5S_B5M80%_T191.6_ENMO_0-24hr + MVPA_E5S_B10M80%_T191.6_ENMO_0-24hr 


Could you please let me know if this thinking is ok?
Or shall I use other data? output 5? 

I have used GGIR package 1.6.0.
I used the code as follows: 

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir="xxx",
             outputdir="xxx",
             f0=1, f1=2,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 2,               ndayswindow= 4,
             hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 0,                 includedaycrit = 16,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(),
             qwindow = c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(),
             mvpathreshold = c(191.6),
             bout.metric = 2,
             closedbout = FALSE,
             desiredtz="Europe/Warsaw",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = TRUE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= c(),
             outliers.only = TRUE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = c(),
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(56.3), threshold.mod = c(191.6),  threshold.vig = c(695.8),
             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),   timewindow = c("WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
             do.report=c(2,5),
             visualreport=TRUE,     dofirstpage =TRUE,
             viewingwindow= 1)

Thank you!
Bart Zalewski

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] MVPA analysis in children
parts:
Hi Bart,

The MVPA output variables from part 2 are not additive, because they try to estimate total time spent in MVPA per day or per week based on different thresholds (bout duration, whether to allow for gaps in bouts, and epoch length). So, you should choose one of them.
Part2 uses by default one specific algorithm (metric) to decide whether to allow for bout gaps, historically originating from the work I did for doi: 10.1093/ije/dyu203.

However, later I realised that an alternative calculation for handling bout gaps is more practical if you want to also characterise light, inactive and vigorous activity in a way that they all can be characterised as non-overlapping categories.
You can activate this alternative calculation (metric) by specifying argument bout.metric=4 in your call to g.shell.GGIR (or g.part2) or by using g.part5 which has bout.metric=4 as a default.

The added value of part5 is that it helps you to split the night time sleep from daytime and it also calculates time spent in light, inactive and vigorous activity. If you are only interested in MVPA and are not concerned about accidentally adding nighttime MVPA (if it exists) then part 2 should be fine.

Best wishes, Vincent
